questions.question: Who designed the administrative code to separate revenue administration from judicial administration?
questions.solution:
• Code: Lord Cornwallis
  • Reform: The Cornwallis Code (1793) is the foundation of the modern Indian Civil Service and police.

questions.question: . The famous Arabic scholar Al Biruni came to contact with India through ________ in the eleventh century A.D.
questions.solution:
• Scholar: Mahmud Ghaznavi
  • Work: Al Biruni wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind', an encyclopedic work on Indian culture and science.

questions.question: ‘A Plan of Economic Development for India’ is also known as ________.
questions.solution:
• Plan: Bombay Plan
  • Economy: Eight Indian capitalists drafted this plan in 1944 for India's post-war development.

questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda Dynasty of Magadha with the help of _______.
questions.solution:
• Help: Vishnugupta
  • Nanda: Chanakya helped Chandragupta destroy the Nanda dynasty and the Greek satraps.

questions.question: When did the All India Congress formalise the demand for ‘Purna Swaraj’ or full independence for India?
questions.solution:
• Independence: At its Lahore Session in 1929
  • Purna Swaraj: The Congress hoisted the tricolour flag on the banks of river Ravi for the first time.

questions.question: The All India Forward Bloc was founded by ________ in 1939 after resigning from the Congress Presidentship.
questions.solution:
• Founder: Subhash Chandra Bose
  • INC: He formed the Forward Bloc to rally left-wing elements within the Congress.

questions.question: In which of the following Vedas was Dasarajna war (the war of ten kings) mentioned?
questions.solution:
• Veda: Rigveda
  • Battle: The Battle of Ten Kings was fought on the banks of the River Parushni (Ravi).

questions.question: Who introduced the system of Dagh and Huliyah and cash payment to soldiers in the Delhi sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Branding: Alauddin Khalji
  • Military: Dagh (branding of horses) and Huliyah (descriptive roll of soldiers) prevented corruption in the army.

questions.question: Who founded the independent State of Bengal?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Murshid Quli Khan
  • Bengal: He moved the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad and became the first Nawab of Bengal.

questions.question: Who was the last king of Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Devabhuti
  • Shunga: He was killed by his minister Vasudeva Kanva, who founded the Kanva dynasty.

questions.question: Iron mines in Jharkhand attributed to the rise of which of the following kingdoms in ancient India?
questions.solution:
• Magadha: Iron mines in Jharkhand
  • Rise: Access to iron ore allowed Magadha to create superior weapons and clear dense forests.

questions.question: Of which of the following Pratihara kings was Rajashekhara, the famous poet and dramatist, the court poet?
questions.solution:
• Court Poet: Mahendrapala
  • Rajashekhara: He was a famous Sanskrit poet who wrote the Karpuramanjari.

questions.question: Name the Bhakti Saint from South India who was initially a Jaina and a minister in the court of a Chalukya king in the twelfth century.
questions.solution:
• Bhakti Saint: Basavanna
  • Movement: He established the Anubhava Mantapa (Hall of Spiritual Experience) in Karnataka.

questions.question: The Mauryan pillar capital found at ________ is popularly known as the Lion Capital.
questions.solution:
• Capital: Sarnath
  • Art: The Lion Capital was built by Ashoka to mark the spot where Buddha first taught the Dhamma.

questions.question: According to Kautilya’s Arthashastra, the Commanding Officer of the cavalry in the Mauryan administration was known as:
questions.solution:
• Officer: Ashwadhyaksha
  • Mauryan: He was responsible for the training and health of the army's horses.

questions.question: The Viceroy who took keen interest in the restoration and protection of historical monuments was _____________.
questions.solution:
• Monuments: Lord Curzon
  • Act: He passed the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act (1904) to protect Indian heritage.

questions.question: For the political education of the people at the local level, who brought the resolution on local self-government?
questions.solution:
• Local Self-Govt: Lord Ripon
  • Reform: He is called the 'Father of Local Self-Government' for establishing municipal boards.

questions.question: Census in India was first started under ________ in the year 1872.
questions.solution:
• Census: Lord Mayo
  • 1872: While Mayo started the census, the first synchronous census was held in 1881 under Ripon.

questions.question: The policy of dual system of government of Bengal was the brainchild of which Governor-General?
questions.solution:
• Dual System: Lord Clive
  • Bengal: Under this, the Company held Diwani (revenue) rights while the Nawab held Nizamat (administration).

questions.question: Who among the following devised a policy that came to be known as the Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.solution:
• Policy: Lord Dalhousie
  • Doctrine: This policy allowed the British to annex states if the ruler died without a natural male heir.

questions.question: Emperor Ashoka conquered Kalinga after how many years of his coronation?
questions.solution:
• Coronation: 8 years
  • Ashoka: The Kalinga War happened in 261 BCE, 8 years after his formal coronation in 269 BCE.

questions.question: During Alauddin Khilji’s reign, the cloth market was known as ________.
questions.solution:
• Market: Sarai-i-Adl
  • Khilji: He created four separate markets in Delhi to control prices strictly.

questions.question: Who was the Mughal emperor during the third battle of Panipat?
questions.solution:
• Battle: Shahalam II
  • Panipat: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler contributed to the revolt of 1857?
questions.solution:
• 1857: Bahadur shah II
  • Mughal: He was proclaimed the Emperor of India by the sepoys before being exiled to Rangoon.

questions.question: Which Kushana ruler was famous in history as a great patron of Buddhism and organised the fourth Buddhist Council?
questions.solution:
• Patron: Kanishka
  • Council: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir and led to the split into Hinayana and Mahayana.

questions.question: Who among the following revolted against Balban, Sultan of Delhi, and declared himself as an independent ruler of Bengal in 1279?
questions.solution:
• Revolt: Tughril Beg
  • Sultanate: Balban personally marched to Bengal to suppress this revolt, the first Sultan to do so.

questions.question: Who among the following was the head of the Diwan-i-Insha department under the Delhi sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Head: Dabir-i-Khas
  • Admin: The Diwan-i-Insha managed all diplomatic and internal state secretarial tasks.

questions.question: Who founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha that was set up to explore spiritual truth?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Debendranath Tagore
  • Sabha: It was established to promote Vedantic monotheism and later merged with the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.question: He was a Delhi Sultan who started the practice of Sijada and Paibos in the court. Who was he?
questions.solution:
• Custom: Ghiyasuddin Balban
  • Court: He modeled his court on the Iranian Sassanid style to project majesty.

questions.question: Who wrote ‘Gift to Monotheists’ in Persian to denounce the belief in many Gods?
questions.solution:
• Work: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
  • Philosophy: Published in 1803, it was a critique of polytheism and priestcraft.
